name: assetkit-models-sf
description: AI photogrammetry-style models of San Francisco landmarks (ships, fountains, bridges), with game-ready LODs

assets.name: Balclutha (1886 full-rigged ship)
assets.description: Steel-hulled three-masted full-rigged ship built 1886 by Charles Connell & Co., Glasgow; museum ship of the San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park at Hyde Street Pier.
assets.notes: Model length (z, 1.0 unit) runs from the bowsprit tip to the stern: 92 m overall (301 ft). The red bottom (antifouling) is about 8% of the length, and she floats light: in the 2012 photo (3-context.jpg) the upper part of the red shows, so the waterline is 4.5 m above the model's lowest point (2026-10-18). Her bow points toward the pier's shore end, by the Eureka (the same photo; about.md's 'north-west' is wrong). Two LODs only: the simplifier stops at ~8 k triangles whatever the error limit (the rigging is hundreds of separate textured strips with UV seams), and most of the memory is the texture; beyond lod1's range a game draws its own stand-in (cityengine: the procedural ship).

assets.name: C.A. Thayer (1895 lumber schooner)
assets.description: Three-masted wooden lumber schooner built 1895 by Hans Bendixsen, Fairhaven CA; museum ship at Hyde Street Pier.
assets.notes: Model x runs over 67 m overall (219 ft, bowsprit and boom). A stray rope stood ~0.24 units out to the side (owner, 2026-10-18: 'may interfere with nearby objects'): cropped at |z| > 0.13 (the hull's half-beam is 0.084, deck fittings reach 0.12). Draft ~3.5 m (depth of hold).

assets.name: Alma (1891 scow schooner)
assets.description: Flat-bottomed San Francisco Bay scow schooner built 1891 at Hunters Point; museum ship of the San Francisco Maritime NHP.
assets.notes: 18 m on deck; the model's z runs from the bowsprit tip past the boom, ~25 m. Its lowest point is the lowered leeboard, ~2.4 m below the hull, so the waterline (1.1 m draft) is ~3.5 m above it. Sails set, as Tripo made her.

assets.name: Hercules (1907 steam tug)
assets.description: Ocean-going steam tug built 1907 by John H. Dialogue & Son, Camden NJ; museum ship at Hyde Street Pier.
assets.notes: 46 m (151 ft); draft 5.5 m aft, ~4.5 m mean.

assets.name: SS Jeremiah O'Brien (1943 Liberty ship)
assets.description: Liberty ship built 1943 at the New England Shipbuilding Corporation, South Portland, Maine; one of two operational Liberty ships, museum ship in San Francisco.
assets.notes: 134.6 m (441 ft 6 in); laden draft 8.5 m, as a museum ship riding higher, ~6 m.

assets.name: USS Pampanito (1943 submarine)
assets.description: Balao-class fleet submarine launched 1943 at Portsmouth Navy Yard; museum ship at Pier 45, Fisherman's Wharf.
assets.notes: 95 m (311 ft 6 in); surfaced draft ~4.6 m; the red bottom is below the waterline. Tripo made her 0.43 units tall to 1.0 long: 41 m at 95 m, against ~17-19 m keel to the top of the periscope shears; squashed in y by 0.47.

assets.name: Taj Mahal houseboat, Sausalito
assets.description: A houseboat in the form of a miniature Taj Mahal, Sausalito.
assets.notes: An easter egg (owner, 2026-10-18). Size estimated (~14 m long on its float); its arched entrance is on -x.

assets.name: Eureka (1890 paddle-wheel ferry)
assets.description: Side-wheel walking-beam passenger and car ferry built 1890 (as Ukiah, rebuilt 1922 as Eureka); museum ship at Hyde Street Pier.
assets.notes: 91 m overall (299 ft 6 in), 24 m over the guards; double-ended, so either end is its front. Model 'based on mini' (owner, 2026-10-18).

assets.name: Victory, Dewey Monument
assets.description: Bronze Victory with trident and wreath on a globe atop the Dewey Monument's column, Union Square (1903).
assets.notes: Untextured: shade as copperoxide (named in the file). Scaled from the owner's photograph (2026-10-18): figure with globe ~2.45 x the shaft's diameter under the capital, which Wikipedia gives as 5 ft (1.5 m): ~3.8 m — a 9 ft figure (Wikipedia) plus the globe; the marker's 'twelve foot' would be the figure with her raised trident. On the 85 ft column (cityengine draws it).

assets.name: Mechanics Monument
assets.description: Bronze group of five mechanics working a punch press, Market and Battery Streets (1901), honouring Peter Donahue.
assets.notes: Untextured: bronze. The model carries the lower granite base; ~7.5 m overall.

assets.name: Mahatma Gandhi, Ferry Building
assets.description: Bronze striding Gandhi with his staff, at the Ferry Building (1988).
assets.notes: Untextured: bronze. 8 ft (2.4 m) striding figure on its rough bronze base (Wikipedia, 'Statue of Mahatma Gandhi (San Francisco)'), on a block with a plaque raised on two steps — a long low block, wider than deep, in the Commons photo (drawn by the renderer).

assets.name: Willie Mays, Oracle Park
assets.description: Bronze Willie Mays at the swing, Willie Mays Plaza, Oracle Park (2000).
assets.notes: Untextured: bronze. The model has its own thin base; on a granite pedestal ~1.5 m (drawn by the renderer).

assets.name: Abraham Lincoln, City Hall
assets.description: Seated bronze Lincoln on the Polk Street side of City Hall (1928).
assets.notes: Untextured: BRONZE (owner's photo, 2026-10-18: 'I was wrong it is actually bronze' — the file name says copperoxide). Seated figure with chair and its base ~2.9 m, on a pale granite die about as tall as the seated figure, a little wider than deep, on a base course (drawn by the renderer).

assets.name: Dewey Monument top (capital and Victory)
assets.description: The top of the Dewey Monument, Union Square (1903): the Corinthian capital, the drum and globe, and the bronze Victory with trident and wreath.
assets.artist: Robert Ingersoll Aitken (figure), Newton J. Tharp (column)
assets.notes: Textured (white stone capital, verdigris figure). Its foot is the capital's neck, 0.208 model units across = the shaft's 5 ft (1.5 m, Wikipedia) under the capital: 7.2 m tall. Sits on a plain cylinder (cityengine draws the shaft). Supersedes dewey-victory (figure only).

assets.name: Dewey Monument top (capital and Victory), PBR
assets.description: The top of the Dewey Monument, Union Square (1903): the Corinthian capital, the drum and globe, and the bronze Victory with trident and wreath.
assets.artist: Robert Ingersoll Aitken (figure), Newton J. Tharp (column)
assets.notes: The same mesh as dewey-monument with Tripo's PBR textures (base colour + metallic-roughness). Packed to compare with the plain textured one (owner, 2026-10-18).

assets.name: Admission Day Monument, the flag-waving miner
assets.description: Bronze young Native Son with a flag over his shoulder, at the foot of the Admission Day Monument column (1897).
assets.notes: Untextured: bronze. The model is the miner and his flag only (no base, no column). 3.2 m is a guess: a ~2.2 m figure plus the raised flag. Front -z: the stride and the head point toward -z in the +x view. The column and Genius figure are not in the model; the granite step it stands on is a 0.9 m plinth.

assets.name: The Cider Press, Golden Gate Park
assets.description: Bronze group of a youth hauling on a cider press lever, a boy crouched at its foot (1892).
assets.notes: Untextured: bronze. 2.5 m (about.md). The model brings its own stone base. Front +z: the +z view shows the youth's chest and hands on the lever; -z shows his back. 15 000/4 000-triangle budget as a group.

assets.name: Ruth Asawa's Andrea fountain figures, Ghirardelli Square
assets.description: Two bronze mermaids with turtles, frogs and lily pads, from the Andrea fountain (1968).
assets.notes: Untextured: bronze. The model is the figures only, no basin, 1.0 x 1.0 units wide. OSM's pool (way 939539789) is 5.2 m across, so 1 unit = 5 m and the height is 0.39 x 5 = 1.9 m (a seated mermaid then ~1.45 m, about.md says ~1.2). No obvious front; +z chosen.

assets.name: Ashurbanipal, Civic Center
assets.description: Bronze Assyrian king Ashurbanipal carrying a lion cub and a tablet, by the Main Library (1988).
assets.notes: Textured (dark bronze, 5 MB jpeg: shrunk to 512/256). Wikipedia: 15 ft (4.6 m) overall; Parhad's site says 8 ft for the figure, so 2.5 m figure on a 2.0 m pedestal. Front -x: the face and tablet show in the -x view. LOD1 would not simplify below ~7.9k triangles at error 0.02 (UV seams), so its error limit is 0.1.

assets.name: Beethoven bust, Music Concourse
assets.description: Bronze bust of Beethoven on a granite pedestal, Golden Gate Park (1915).
assets.notes: Untextured: bronze. The model is the bust with a small socle (~1.3 m, about.md says ~1 m bust); the tall granite shaft with the muse is a 2.2 m plinth. Front -x (the face in the -x view).

assets.name: Benjamin Franklin, Washington Square
assets.description: Bronze Franklin in 18th-century dress holding a paper, on a tall granite drinking-fountain pedestal (1879).
assets.notes: Untextured: bronze. The file is named city_hall but the about.md (Washington Square) is the one used; a standing coat-and-breeches Franklin with a paper in hand matches both. 2.4 m figure on a ~3.4 m granite pedestal. Front -x.

assets.name: Bufano's St. Francis, Fisherman's Wharf
assets.description: Monolithic hooded granite St. Francis with arms spread, at Taylor and Beach (Frank Cresci Plaza).
assets.notes: Untextured: the granite is drawn as concrete. 18 ft (5.5 m), 12-20 tons of granite (Kerouac.com, HMDB). The model has its own tapered base. Front -x (the hooded face shows in the -x view).

assets.name: Bufano's Peace, Brotherhood Way
assets.description: Bufano's 38 ft Peace (1958): a hooded stainless-steel figure with gold leaf, granite and tile mosaic, a gift of the San Francisco Chronicle; first at the airport, since 1996 beside the dog park on Brotherhood Way.
assets.notes: Textured. About 38 ft (11.6 m) overall (SF Arts Commission / ARG Conservation). The model has its own round base. Front -x (the face and rose robe show in the -x view). Peace stands at 800 Brotherhood Way, inside San Francisco (SFO was its first home).

assets.name: Bufano's Penguins, Gateway Commons
assets.description: Bufano's simplified granite penguin with a small chick at its feet and a red-capped beak, on an octagonal base.
assets.notes: Textured (grey granite, red beak). About 1.8 m including its octagonal base (about.md says 1.5-2 m; the base is part of the model). Front +z (the chick and crossed feet show in the +z view).

assets.name: Cervantes Monument, Golden Gate Park
assets.description: Jo Mora's Cervantes Monument (1916): a bronze bust on a granite boulder, Don Quixote and Sancho Panza kneeling at its foot.
assets.notes: Textured. About 3.5 m overall (about.md: 3-3.5 m, bust and boulder). The boulder is its own base. Front -z: the bust's collar, the scroll and the kneeling figures face -z.

assets.name: General Pershing, Golden Gate Park
assets.description: Haig Patigian's bronze General Pershing (1922), a German helmet at his feet, on a tall granite pedestal at the Music Concourse.
assets.notes: Untextured: bronze. The figure is about 2.6 m with its thin base; the granite pedestal (~3.2 m) is drawn by the renderer. Front -z (the face and the helmet's side show in the -z view).

assets.name: Chinatown guardian lion, Dragon Gate
assets.description: Seated Chinese guardian lion (shishi) in carved granite, one of the pair at the Dragon Gate, Grant Avenue at Bush.
assets.notes: Untextured: granite drawn as concrete. One model, placed twice (a pair, mirrored in bearing). Front -x (the face shows in the -x view). 1.4 m including its own base, on a ~0.6 m pedestal.

assets.name: Goddess of Democracy, Portsmouth Square
assets.description: Bronze woman holding a torch aloft in both hands, a 1994 replica of the Tiananmen Square 'Goddess of Democracy', in Portsmouth Square, Chinatown.
assets.artist: Thomas Marsh and Shanghai/Beijing Central Academy of Fine Arts students (replica of the 1989 Tiananmen statue)
assets.notes: Untextured: bronze. About 3 m including the model's own thin slab; the real figure stands on a pale granite block about 0.9 m high (Commons photo), drawn by the renderer. Front -x (torch at the left, hair swept right in the -x view, as in the Commons 3/4 photo).

assets.name: Joseph Strauss, Golden Gate Bridge
assets.description: Bronze Joseph B. Strauss, chief engineer of the Golden Gate Bridge, in a three-piece suit with rolled plans, on the Strauss Legacy Circle at the bridge's south end.
assets.notes: Untextured: bronze. ~2.5 m figure including the model's own small bronze slab; it stands on a low round grey disc (Legacy Circle, ~0.4 m) which is not drawn. Front -x (tie and plans show in the -x view).

assets.name: The Lone Sailor, Vista Point
assets.description: Bronze US Navy sailor in a peacoat with a sea bag on a bollard, on a red granite plinth: the Lone Sailor replica at Vista Point beside the Golden Gate Bridge.
assets.notes: Textured; the model carries its own red polished granite base (the figure ~2.1 m on a ~0.4 m base: 2.5 m overall). Front -x (face and sea bag toward the camera in the -x view, as in the Commons photos).

assets.name: Lotta's Fountain
assets.description: The cast-iron fountain column at Market, Geary and Kearny Streets, given to the city by the actress Lotta Crabtree in 1875.
assets.notes: Textured, bronze-coloured. About 24 ft (7.3 m) overall, the whole fountain column including its base (Wikipedia gives no height; the earlier procedural stand-in used 8 m with a 0.5 m offset). Four-sided, so the front is arbitrary (+z).

assets.name: Miguel Hidalgo, Dolores Park
assets.description: Bronze standing Father Miguel Hidalgo in a long coat and boots, one arm out, at the upper corner of Dolores Park (1962).
assets.notes: Untextured: bronze. ~3 m figure on a small rock base (the model has it); stands on a tall black granite die (~2.6 m) on a low black platform (drawn by the renderer from the Commons photo). Face seen from -x.

assets.name: Pioneer Mother, Golden Gate Park
assets.description: Bronze mother with two children, arm outstretched, on the stepped top of Grafly's 1915 monument (moved to Golden Gate Park in 1940).
assets.notes: Untextured: bronze. The model has the small stepped bronze top (~3 m figure, 3.3 m with it); the tall red-brown stone base with the ship relief (about 3.3 m of the ~7.9 m total) is the plinth. Face seen from -x.

assets.name: Puddle Jumpers, Transamerica Redwood Park
assets.description: Five bronze children running and leaping in a chain through a puddle, Transamerica Redwood Park.
assets.notes: Untextured: bronze. Chain of five, ~3.2 m long (children ~1.1 m, the leader leaping); no base. Leader (arm flung out) is at -z, so the group runs toward -z.

assets.name: Seal balancing a ball, Seals Plaza
assets.description: Bronze seal balancing a ball on its nose, on a ring base, in Seals Plaza at Oracle Park's Marina Gate.
assets.notes: Untextured: bronze. The file is named Lou Seal (the Giants mascot); the model is a seal balancing a ball on a split-ring base, which matches the Seals Plaza sculpture outside the ballpark, so it is placed there. Height ~2 m is a guess (no source gives it). Head toward -z.

assets.name: Crab topiary, Pier 39
assets.description: Dark crab with raised claws, its shell planted with flowers: the crab topiary at Pier 39.
assets.notes: Textured. Height ~2.5 m is a guess (no source found); front taken as -x (claws up toward the viewer).

assets.name: Guardians of the Gate sea lions, Pier 39
assets.description: Everdur bronze family of sea lions on a rock base, West Park beside Pier 39 (1992).
assets.notes: Untextured: bronze. The model carries its own rock base. Real size 4 ft 6 in x 8 ft x 5 ft (public-art list; which is height is not stated), so 1.4 m high. Front +x (guess: the two animals face that way).

assets.name: Spanish bronze cannon, Presidio
assets.description: Spanish bronze cannon on a concrete block, as on the Presidio's Main Post (Pershing Square and the Officers' Club).
assets.notes: Textured. Barrel ~2.3 m (guess: NPS gives no length); the model has its concrete mounting block. Muzzle toward +z (bore seen from +z).

assets.name: Robert Louis Stevenson Memorial galleon, Portsmouth Square
assets.description: The bronze galleon with sails set on its carved wave base, the finial of the Robert Louis Stevenson Memorial in Portsmouth Square.
assets.notes: Textured. The model is only the ship and its carved base (the granite shaft, ~10 ft, is drawn by the procedural stevensonMemorial), so it is attached on top of that shaft. Ship long axis is z with the bowsprit at +z (front). 1.1 m overall height is a guess (no source gives it): the procedural stand-in's galleon is ~1 m long. A monument finial, not a boat: it floats on nothing.

assets.name: Roman Gladiator, Golden Gate Park
assets.description: Bronze gladiator with a raised short sword and flowing cloak, on a granite pedestal with a bronze plaque, beside the de Young Museum (the 1894 Midwinter Fair commemoration).
assets.notes: Textured; the model carries its own pedestal (about 40% of the height). about.md: ~2.5 m bronze figure on a stone pedestal; with the pedestal as drawn (photo 1-front.jpg: figure about 60% of the whole) that is ~4.2 m overall. Front +z: the sword-arm and outstretched arm point to +z and the cloak streams to -z; the plaque is on the +z face.
